title: How to celebrate a festival with children · AquaTerra
description: How AquaTerra celebrates festivals with children: carols, crafts, masks and colours, one activity a session, a small team. {count} drives since {firstYear}.
lede: AquaTerra celebrates festivals with children through short workshops: carols and masks at Christmas, colours at Holi, rakhis at Raksha Bandhan and crafts for Durga Puja. Students have run {count} of these festival drives since {firstYear}, with {volunteers} volunteer turnouts, and Christmas is the festival we run most often.

sections.heading: pick a festival and one activity
body: Choose one festival and one activity that children can finish in a single session. Our festival drives have used carols, card-making, masks, wrapping paper, rakhis, diyas and Holi colours. The titles tell the plan at a glance: Christmas Carols Workshop, Santa Mask Making, Rakhi Moments and Holi Hues. The activity should be something children can take home or perform.

Christmas is the festival we run most often. The longest series was Merry Miracles, five days from 15 to 25 December 2023, and each day had its own activity: crafts, a dental checkup, a Santa mask competition, a carnival and a movie outing. Give each day of a series a clear name, as Merry Miracles did.

sections.heading: where it happens
body: Most festival drives ran at {topPlace}, the Sunday school where many of our Christmas, Durga Puja and Holi sessions were held. Ek Tara and AIM Foundation hosted several more, and a few were held at other places, including Tetultala Ashram, Calcutta Rescue and Newtown.
Check the room with the host a few days before, especially if the day needs space for carols, a carnival or a competition.

sections.heading: on the day
body: A festival day mixes making and singing. The Christmas Carnival Workshop at Pather Sathi in December 2024 had games, music, crafts and treats. At Merry Masks, children made paper masks and sang carols. Start with the making, then the singing, then something to share, which is how the December 2025 carols session ended, with cake and classic festive stories.

Holi and Durga Puja followed the same shape. Splash of Joy in March 2024 at Pather Sathi was a Holi workshop of colours and crafts, and Holi Hues in March 2025 used organic colours with seven volunteers. The Colours Of Durga series ran five sessions at Pather Sathi between late September and early October 2023. Keep the colours and materials simple where you can.

sections.heading: keep it simple and green
body: Festival craft can be simple and kind to the environment. Green Christmas at Ek Tara in December 2021 swapped plastic for plants and crafts. At Secret Cheer in December 2024, the children made their own wrapping paper, and volunteers wrapped gifts in it for a secret Santa game later with the children.

Paper is the common material. Rakhi Moments at Ek Tara in August 2024 had students make rakhis, and Sacred Strings at BSS school in August 2025 taught rakhi making to two hundred children. Paper masks, cards and wrapping paper filled several December sessions too.

sections.heading: after the festival
body: Write the festival up while it is fresh, with the day, the place, the activity and the team. A series reads clearly when each day has its own write-up, as Merry Miracles does across its numbered days, so the next team can see what each day involved.

Plan the next festival early. A Christmas series can start in early December and finish on the day, as Merry Miracles did in 2023 and again in 2025 across three days. A Durga Puja series can start in September, as the Colours Of Durga did.

sections.heading: join a festival team
body: Members run these festival drives, and students aged 14 to 19 can join. Sign in with Google to start, and your membership is approved before you take part. If you would like to bring a festival session to a school or group, start on the [collaborations page](/collaborations), or [join AquaTerra](/join) to help with the next one.

learnings: One festival and one activity per session gives children a clear job, such as a Santa mask or a handful of Holi colours.
A festival can run as a series with a different activity each day, as Merry Miracles did across five days in 2023.
Christmas leads this page, so plan the December calendar early.
Keep materials simple and natural, from wrapping paper the children made to organic colours for Holi.
Close with something shared, such as cake after carols, which is how the December 2025 session at Pather Sathi ended.

faqs.q: How do you celebrate a festival with children in Kolkata?
faqs.a: Pick one festival and one activity that children can finish in a single session, such as carols, masks, rakhis or Holi colours. AquaTerra has run {count} festival drives since {firstYear}, mostly with students at Pather Sathi and other host places across the city.

faqs.q: What do children do at an AquaTerra Christmas workshop?
faqs.a: They make cards and masks, learn and sing carols, take part in quizzes and games, and make wrapping paper. The Merry Miracles series ran five days in December 2023, with crafts, a dental checkup, a Santa mask competition, a carnival and a movie outing.

faqs.q: Does AquaTerra run Holi and Durga Puja workshops for children?
faqs.a: Yes. Holi sessions included Splash of Joy at Pather Sathi in March 2024 and Holi Hues in March 2025, which used organic colours. The Durga Puja series, Colours Of Durga, ran as five sessions at Pather Sathi in autumn 2023.

faqs.q: How many volunteers do festival workshops need?
faqs.a: Most festival workshops had between two and six volunteers, and a few had more. Across this page, {volunteers} volunteer turnouts went into the drives, counting each time someone showed up.

faqs.q: Can a school host an AquaTerra festival workshop?
faqs.a: Schools have hosted festival workshops, including the Rakhi Loom session at South Calcutta Inner Wheel School in August 2023 and Sacred Strings at BSS school in August 2025. Get in touch through the collaborations page to talk about a session.
